high.why: rule-based document review with money attached
classification into a standard code set

reads_text.text: Is the core of `task` reading or reviewing written or digital information, such as documents, forms, messages, records, listings, transcripts or code, to reach a judgment?

criteria.true: Most of the work is reading information and judging it.
criteria.false: Most of the work is physical, conversational, creative, or done with tools or equipment.

closed_outcome.text: Does `task` end in a decision picked from a small, known set of outcomes, such as approve or deny, a category, a priority level, match or no match, or a ranking?

criteria.true: The result is one pick from a known set of options.
criteria.false: The result is new written content, a design, a conversation, or a physical change.

writes_content.text: Does `task` produce a new document, such as a report, letter, article, plan, proposal or program code, as its main result?

criteria.true: The main result is a new document or code written by the worker.
criteria.false: The main result is a decision, a check, a physical result or a conversation; any writing is notes or form-filling.

physical.text: How much of `task` is physical, hands-on work?
criteria: None: all of it can be done at a desk or computer.
A little: mostly desk work with occasional hands-on steps.
Mostly hands-on work with some desk work.
All hands-on: handling objects, people, tools, vehicles or equipment.

live_human.text: Is talking with people in real time, in person or by phone, the main activity in `task`?

criteria.true: Most of the task is live conversation: interviewing, advising, teaching, selling, negotiating or serving someone.
criteria.false: Most of the task is done without live conversation.

same_rules.text: In `task`, does the worker apply a fixed set of written rules, policies, standards or checklists to each item?

criteria.true: Each item is checked against the same fixed standard.
criteria.false: Items are handled with custom judgment, creativity or open-ended problem solving, or the task does not judge items.

errors_lose_money.text: Can a mistake in `task` directly cost the organization money, for example by paying too much, charging too little, paying a fraudulent claim or incurring a penalty?

loss_recoverable.text: If a mistake in `task` loses money, can that money usually be found and recovered later, as with overpayments, duplicate payments, billing errors or clawed-back fraud?

criteria.true: Lost money can be found and recovered later.
criteria.false: Lost money is gone, or mistakes do not lose money.

outcome_visible.text: Is it later possible to see whether a judgment made in `task` was right, from a real outcome such as a payment, an appeal result, a sale, or an error found later?

criteria.true: Real outcomes later show whether each judgment was right.
criteria.false: There is no later outcome that shows whether a judgment was right.

speed_value.text: Would finishing `task` in minutes instead of hours or days reduce waiting for customers, payments or decisions?

criteria.true: Faster completion clearly reduces delays or captures value.
criteria.false: Speed matters little because the task runs on a schedule, needs someone present, or is limited by quality rather than time.

digital_input.text: What form do the inputs to `task` usually take?

criteria.digital_text: Emails, database records, electronic forms, documents or code on a computer
criteria.images_or_audio: Photos, scans, drawings, video, audio or speech
criteria.physical_objects: Physical objects, materials, machines or places

licensed_signoff.text: Each judgment in `task` legally requires sign-off from a licensed professional.

time_per_item.text: Can a trained worker finish one item of `task` in a few minutes or less?

volume.text: How often does one worker handle a new item in `task`?
criteria: Now and then: the task comes up occasionally or as one-off projects.
All day long from a steady queue.
A constant, fast stream where each item takes moments.

money_link.text: How directly does getting `task` right or wrong affect money?
criteria: Indirect: it affects efficiency, quality or satisfaction.
Direct: it decides payments, prices, claims, refunds, fraud or revenue.
Large and direct: a single judgment can move thousands of dollars or more.
